description: A pixel office for your OpenClaw: turn invisible work states into a cozy little space with characters, daily notes, and guest agents. Code under MIT; art assets for non-commercial learning only.

summary.one_liner: A pixel-art AI office dashboard (Flask backend, Phaser frontend) that visualizes AI agent work states, daily notes, and guest agents in a cozy virtual office.
summary.what_it_does: Shows an AI assistant's current work state as an animated pixel character moving between office zones, with bubbles and status text. It maps six states (idle, writing, researching, executing, syncing, error) to areas of the office. It reads recent work notes from memory/*.md and shows them as a "yesterday notes" card with sensitive content redacted. Other agents can join through a join key and push their status every 15 seconds via a provided script. The UI is available in Chinese, English, and Japanese, works on mobile, and includes sidebar password protection. Optional features include AI image generation for backgrounds via the Gemini API and an Electron desktop-pet wrapper. States are set through set_state.py or HTTP endpoints such as POST /set_state.
use_cases: Monitor what an AI agent is doing in real time
Show team or multi-agent status on a shared dashboard
Personal pixel-art status page for remote work
Drive office status from scripts or HTTP requests
Give guest agents a way to report status into a shared office
Expose a status board publicly via Cloudflare Tunnel
how_to_run: python3 set_state.py writing "正在整理文档"
notable: Designed for OpenClaw agents, with a SKILL.md deployment flow and SOUL.md status-sync rules
Guest agents join via join keys, with up to 3 concurrent users per key by default
Stale states automatically revert to idle
Optional Electron desktop pet with transparent window
caveats: Art assets are licensed for non-commercial learning and demo use only; code is MIT
Requires Python 3.10+ (uses X | Y union type syntax)
Desktop pet mode is experimental and mainly tested on macOS
Best experience with OpenClaw; standalone use requires manually pushing states
